messages.subject: [R-pkg-devel] Winbuilder issue on R API checks
messages.subject_clean: [R-pkg-devel] Winbuilder issue on R API checks
messages.body_plain:
I believe that there is an issue with Winbuilder failing the R API checks for compiled code.  I got a NOTE for a package submission:


* checking compiled code ... NOTE
Error in ccE(lines, flags = new_flags, include = include) :
  'cc' is not on the path
Calls: <Anonymous> ... lapply -> FUN -> lapply -> FUN -> getFunsHdr -> ccE
Execution halted


See 'Writing portable packages' in the 'Writing R Extensions' manual.
* checking installed files from 'inst/doc' ? OK

That seems to be coming from `cc` not being found in tools:::ccE() (src/library/tools/R/apitools.R) which invokes the C preprocessor as the literal command cc (via Sys.which("cc?))

Environment variable not being set?

As a check I uploaded an existing package on CRAN to Winbuilder and it ran into the same issue.

-Naras

messages.subject_clean: [R-pkg-devel] CRAN NOTE Found the following files/directories: ‘~/tmp/scratch/Rtmp...’
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

Jut recently, I got a CRAN NOTE on all of my packages (<https://cran.rstudio.com/web/checks/check_results_pepijn.devries_at_outlook.com.html>):

>? Found the following files/directories: ?~/tmp/scratch/Rtmp...?

Is this a new check implemented on the CRAN check machines, or is it just a quirk?

I've started inspecting one of my simpler and light-weight packages (opensimplex2), and I'm pretty sure it doesn't write to the tempdir (or anywhere else). If this is not a quirk, how can I reproduce the check-result and trace the problem?

Suggestions are welcome.

Cheers,

Pepijn

messages.body_plain:
Dear Kurt,

The temporary files created for Xvfb seem to interfere with the check
for new files on the r-devel-linux-x86_64-debian-gcc machine. Almost
all packages got a NOTE. Apologies if you've already received messages
about this.

On Sun, 2 Aug 2026 09:31:45 +0000
Pepijn de Vries <pepijn.devries at outlook.com> wrote:

> >? Found the following files/directories: ?~/tmp/scratch/Rtmp...?  
> 
> Is this a new check implemented on the CRAN check machines, or is it
> just a quirk?

Must be a quirk: it affects almost all packages on one of the machines.

tools::CRAN_check_details() -> db
db |> with(aggregate(
 grepl('Found the following files/directories', Output),
 list(Flavor = Flavor, Package = Package),
 max
)) |> aggregate(
 x ~ Flavor, data = _,
 \(x) round(mean(x)*100)
)

                              Flavor   x
1  r-devel-linux-x86_64-debian-clang   0
2    r-devel-linux-x86_64-debian-gcc 100
3  r-devel-linux-x86_64-fedora-clang   0
4    r-devel-linux-x86_64-fedora-gcc   0

6               r-oldrel-macos-arm64   0
7              r-oldrel-macos-x86_64   0
8            r-oldrel-windows-x86_64   0
9             r-patched-linux-x86_64   0
10            r-release-linux-x86_64   0
11             r-release-macos-arm64   0
12            r-release-macos-x86_64   0
13          r-release-windows-x86_64   0

-- 
Best regards,
Ivan
